questions.question: How long does the built-in `browser` fixture live?
options: One test
One test file
One worker process
The whole test run, across all workers
questions.explanation: `browser` is worker-scoped. Tests in a worker share it, and each test gets its own `context` for isolation.

questions.question: A fixture calls `use(value)` without `await`. What happens?
options: The code after `use()` runs before the test body, and the test can still pass
Playwright refuses to load the test file
The fixture is set up twice
The test always times out
questions.explanation: Nothing waits for the test to finish, so cleanup runs too early and no error is reported.

questions.question: Why does a worker-scoped fixture that asks for `page` fail?
options: Worker fixtures can't have dependencies
`page` only works inside `beforeEach`
It needs `{ auto: true }` as well
`page` is test-scoped, so it can't outlive a single test
questions.explanation: A worker fixture can depend only on other worker fixtures. Build what you need from `browser` or `playwright` instead.

questions.question: A fixture listens to `page.on('console')` for errors. What does it miss?
options: Calls to `console.error()`
Uncaught exceptions, which fire `pageerror`
Errors logged during page load
Errors logged after the first navigation
questions.explanation: An uncaught exception doesn't produce a console event. Listen to `pageerror` as well.

questions.question: What does `{ auto: true }` do to a fixture?
options: It shares the fixture across workers
It retries the fixture when setup fails
It runs the fixture for every test, even when no test asks for it
It lets `test.use()` override the fixture's value
questions.explanation: Automatic fixtures suit checks that should always run. `option: true` is the setting that makes a value configurable.
